# Shaft i-J-k

This is Basic Block Catalog type `420` (`Shaft i-J-k`). It represents a mechanical or drive-train relation used by rotating-machine models.

<!-- veragrid-block-introduction:start -->
**Shaft i-J-k** belongs to an electromechanical machine or prime-mover model. It links electrical torque and flux with rotor speed, angle, mechanical power, or actuator dynamics, making it central to frequency, voltage, and rotor-angle stability studies.

## Typical use

- Use it when electrical transients must interact with rotating mass or machine controls.
- Initialize torque, power, flux, and speed consistently with the solved power flow.
<!-- veragrid-block-introduction:end -->

## Behaviour

- Library location: `Native / Mechanical / Drive Train`.
- Inputs: 3.
- Outputs: 2.
- Declared states: 0.
- Configurable parameters: 6.
- The imported definition is fully supported by the Dynamic Editor catalogue.

## Characteristic equations

$$
xdtheta_{jk}(t_0) = (\frac{1}{K_{jk}} \cdot (torque_{ij} - D_{jj} \cdot omega_{j}))
$$

$$
xomega_{j}(t_0) = omega_{k}
$$

## Interface table

| Category | Name | Meaning | Units |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Input | `omega_k` | Input signal consumed by the block | model-dependent |
| Input | `omega_i` | Input signal consumed by the block | model-dependent |
| Input | `torque_ij` | Input signal consumed by the block | model-dependent |
| Output | `omega_j` | Output signal produced by the block | model-dependent |
| Output | `torque_jk` | Output signal produced by the block | model-dependent |
| Parameter | `K_jk` | Configurable model parameter | model-dependent |
| Parameter | `D_jk` | Configurable model parameter | model-dependent |
| Parameter | `D_ij` | Configurable model parameter | model-dependent |
| Parameter | `D_jj` | Configurable model parameter | model-dependent |
| Parameter | `H_j` | Configurable model parameter | model-dependent |
| Parameter | `fnom` | Configurable model parameter | model-dependent |

## Editing notes

Use General options for numeric parameter values and the DAE tab for symbolic variables and equations. Changing an Output flag only controls whether a variable is exported; it does not remove the variable from the model.
